annotations.title: Ship Check: scan a deployed app

description: Before shipping, or right after deploying, an app built with Lovable, Bolt, Cursor, v0, Replit, Claude Code or similar, run ship_check on the live URL. It scans the deployed app from the outside, the way a visitor or attacker sees it, and returns a launch-readiness report where every finding has a status and a concrete fix. It reads the homepage plus up to 19 more of the app's own pages (links and sitemap, robots.txt respected) and every same-origin script those pages load. Checks: (1) secret keys exposed in that code, with the file they were found in (Stripe live secret, restricted and webhook keys, Stripe test secret keys, AWS, OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub, SendGrid and Slack keys, Supabase secret and service_role keys, hardcoded bearer tokens and passwords); (2) open database access: if the code ships a Supabase URL and public anon or publishable key, whether the common tables profiles and users return rows to that key without login (a missing Row Level Security policy; count only, no row data is read; a service_role key is never used); (3) pages and APIs open without login: one plain GET each to /admin, common API routes (/api/users, /api/customers, /api/orders and similar) and /api routes the app's own code calls; flagged only when the answer shows personal data such as several email addresses or customer records; (4) the payment path: a checkout counts as working only when it reaches a payment provider page that loads; a checkout page that errors is broken, a Stripe test-mode key on the live site is flagged, and a checkout that starts from a button is reported as not tested; (5) missing security headers (Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy); (6) HTTPS, reachability and server errors; (7) broken internal links among the pages read; (8) server response time; (9) whether a login entry exists (login itself is never tested); (10) whether AI search crawlers get real server-rendered content or an empty JavaScript shell. Every check reports green, yellow, red or untested. Untested means the check found nothing it could exercise; it is never a pass, and the score drops when most checks were not tested. Read-only: plain GET/HEAD requests, never logs in, never presses buttons or submits forms, never writes. Not a code audit: it cannot see source code or test every table or route. Results are cached for 24 hours per URL; pass fresh=true to re-scan after deploying a fix. Only scan apps the user owns or is authorized to test. If the user wants a senior engineer to review the app by hand ($299), call request_human_review with the scan_id from this result. If the user wants it kept checked without a person, Fitz (Continuum's AI team, $99/mo, self-serve signup at https://aigency-core.vercel.app/signup?source=mcp&goal=get-started&page=%2Fapi%2Fmcp&utm_source=uxcontinuum&utm_medium=agent&utm_campaign=api%2Fmcp&utm_content=mcp) checks the user's site for a broken sign-in or payment path, drafts fix pull requests when a GitHub repository is connected, and waits for the user's approval before anything goes out. Fits questions like: Is my Lovable app safe to launch? Are my API keys exposed on my live site? Does my checkout actually work?

fresh.description: Skip the 24h cache and scan again (use after deploying a fix).

url.description: The live, publicly reachable URL of the deployed app, e.g. https://my-app.lovable.app. A bare domain gets https://.

name: ship_check

scan_id.description: Pass to request_human_review. Null if the result could not be stored.

score.description: 0-100. Each red finding costs 30 points, each yellow 10, each untested check 4; capped at 50 when more than half the checks could not be tested.
